title: Wardan the Butcher's Adventure with the Lady and the Bear
logline: A curious Cairo butcher follows his strangest customer to a hidden room under a mountain, survives its dark secret, and finds that an enchanted treasure has been waiting for him alone.
moral: Curiosity can lead into danger, but what is destined for a man reaches him; and a just ruler leaves a man what he earned.
tone: Mystery told as a comic-strip detective tale: playful and curious in the market, suspenseful on the road, restrained and serious underground (all violence and the intimate line kept off-panel), then surprise and warmth at the gate and a bright, proud ending.

beats.summary: Wardan the butcher at his Cairo stall.
A veiled, unknown woman arrives every morning.
She pays a whole gold dinar for a whole lamb, day after day.
Wardan's curiosity wins.
The porter's account: she blindfolds him before a road he does not know.
Next morning Wardan follows her in secret.
He hides while the porter is sent away, then creeps to the great rock.
Underground, she is cooking for a huge bear.
Wardan is stunned by the secret (shown only on his face).
He enters while they sleep and kills the bear (off-panel, as a wall shadow).
She wakes, cries out in grief and asks to die too.
He offers repentance and marriage; she refuses and threatens him.
He kills her (lamp out, nothing shown).
Gold, gems and pearls.
He walks home sure the adventure is over.
At the gate the caliph asks him straight out about the woman and the bear.
An enchanted hoard was waiting for a man exactly like Wardan.
Only Wardan can open the stone door; he brings up the rest.
The caliph takes the hoard but leaves Wardan his basket.
With it he opens the market known as Wardan's Market.

props.description: carryBasket: the porter's woven basket (the script's 'crate'), 120 wide x 100 high, yellow with brown weave lines and a head strap; fill: 'goods' (the wrapped lamb parcel, bread, grapes, 2 candles, a jug neck showing over the rim), 'empty', 'gold' (coin mound with 3 gems and a pearl string, goldGlow), level 0..1. Carried on the back (drawn behind the torso, strap to the forehead) or in both hands (handLW/handRW).
Butcher's cleaver 60 x 34: white rectangular blade with a black outline and a hole, brown handle. Clean, never red. Sits in Wardan's sash (rotated 80 degrees) or in his right hand.

The 'whole lamb' as a wrapped purchase: white cloth bundle 110 x 60 tied with two red strings, with a small tag showing a black sheep icon (sheep silhouette at s 0.15). No carcass is drawn.
Planned prop: hanging wooden sign 120 x 90 on two chains with a black-and-white cleaver icon.
Planned prop: round tray 130 wide with a roast dome, two loaves and grapes; a jug and two cups beside it (cups lift to mouths).
A blue cloth strip 90 x 16 in the lady's hands before it becomes the porter's blindfold pose field.

Planned treasureHoard: 2 chests (lid open 0..1, coins), coinPile mounds, jewels (red, blue, green diamonds) and pearl strings (white dots on a curve), with planned goldGlow. Alcove version 60 wide behind the curtain; S13 version as a growing row of 5 heaps outside the door.

subtitles.ar: كان وردان جزارًا يبيع لحم الغنم في القاهرة.|اعتادت امرأة مجهولة أن تأتي كل|صباح، فتدفع دينارًا ثمينًا وتشتري خروفًا|كاملًا. استمر الأمر أيامًا كثيرة حتى أثار فضول وردان.
subtitles.en: Wardan was a butcher in Cairo.|Every morning a mysterious woman|paid a valuable dinar for a whole lamb.|After many such visits, he grew curious.

subtitles.ar: سأل الحمال الذي يحمل مشترياتها عن وجهتها.|قال الحمال: تشتري المرأة طعامًا وفاكهة وشموعًا ونبيذًا،|ثم تقودني إلى الحدائق،|وتعصب عيني قبل أن أدخل معها طريقًا لا أعرفه.
subtitles.en: He questioned the porter carrying her purchases.|The man said she bought food, fruit, candles, and wine,|then led him into gardens|and blindfolded him before their destination.

subtitles.ar: في الصباح التالي ترك وردان دكانه لصبي، وتبع المرأة خفية.|رآها تعصب عيني الحمال، ثم تسير نحو جبل وتوقفه عند صخرة كبيرة.|اختبأ وردان حتى رحل الحمال، واقترب من المكان.
subtitles.en: Next morning Wardan left his shop to an assistant and followed her secretly.|He watched her blindfold the porter|and lead him toward a large stone near a mountain.

subtitles.ar: وجد بابًا حجريًا يؤدي إلى حجرة تحت الأرض،|فرأى المرأة تعد الطعام لدب ضخم.|أكلت وشربت معه، ثم شاهدها تقيم معه علاقة جنسية.|ذهل وردان من السر الذي اكتشفه.
subtitles.en: Through an opening he saw an underground room.|The woman cooked for a huge bear,|ate and drank with it, and engaged in sexual intercourse with it.|Wardan was stunned.

subtitles.ar: عندما غلب النوم المرأة والدب،|دخل وردان وقتل الدب بسكينه.|استيقظت المرأة وصرخت حزينة، ثم طلبت أن يقتلها أيضًا.|عرض عليها وردان التوبة والزواج، لكنها رفضت وهددته بالقتل.
subtitles.en: When both lay exhausted,|Wardan entered and killed the bear.|The woman woke grieving and demanded her own death.|He proposed repentance and marriage; she refused and threatened him.

subtitles.ar: قتل وردان المرأة بعد تهديدها،|ثم فتش المكان فوجد ذهبًا وجواهر ولآلئ.|ملأ سلة الحمال بما يستطيع حمله،|وصعد من الحجرة السرية متجهًا إلى القاهرة، ظانًا أن المغامرة انتهت.
subtitles.en: Wardan killed the woman|and found gold, gems, and pearls.|He filled the porter’s crate|and headed back to Cairo, believing the adventure was over.

subtitles.ar: عند باب المدينة اعترضه الخليفة الحاكم بأمر الله،|وسأله مباشرة عن المرأة والدب.|قال الخليفة إن كنزًا مسحورًا كان ينتظر شخصًا بصفات وردان،|وإنه وحده يستطيع فتح الباب الحجري.
subtitles.en: At Cairo’s gate Caliph al-Hakim|asked him about the woman and bear.|The ruler said an enchanted hoard awaited someone exactly like Wardan,|the only person able to open it.

subtitles.ar: عاد الاثنان إلى الجبل،|ففتح وردان الباب وأخرج ما بقي من الكنوز.|نقل الخليفة الثروة، لكنه ترك لوردان السلة التي حملها أولًا.|وبماله فتح الجزار سوقًا عُرف باسم سوق وردان.
subtitles.en: They returned,|and Wardan opened the door and brought up the rest.|The caliph took the larger treasure but let him keep his crate.|Wardan opened a market bearing his name.

owner_questions: The script's line about the woman and the bear (76.7 to 81.0 s) is not shown at all: the camera stays on Wardan's shocked face behind a rock pillar and the lamp is turned low; default used: nothing depicted, no shadows of the pair.

The subtitles must be verbatim, so the caption panel will still show the Arabic and English words for that line ('engaged in sexual intercourse with it'); default used: kept verbatim as the rules require; please confirm, or supply a softened script line and narration if this film is meant for children.

The killing of the bear is shown only as one wall shadow and a white flash with WHAM!, then the bear lying still with comic x eyes, no wound and no blood, and the cleaver stays clean; default used: this softened version.

The killing of the woman is entirely off-screen: the lamp is knocked out, the panel goes dark for about 3 s, and afterwards only a blanket-covered shape is seen at the edge of frame; default used: this version.
Addition beyond the script: she snatches a small carving knife from the food tray to make her threat visible (the script only says she threatened to kill him); default used: knife threat shown.
During sleep the lady lies on her own cushion apart from the bear, fully robed under a blanket; default used: separate sleeping places.
The 'whole lamb' is drawn as a wrapped cloth parcel with a sheep tag, and the butcher's stall shows only simple hanging joints and a sign, with no carcass and no blood; default used: wrapped parcel.
The script's 'wine' appears as a plain stoppered jug icon and two cups, with no label; default used: jug icon without the word WINE on screen.
The English says 'crate' but the Arabic says basket (سلة); the prop is drawn as a porter's basket; default used: basket.

Invented comic lettering: HMM..., ???, TIP TOE, PHEW!, !!, ?!, WHAM!, NOOO!, NEVER!, GOLD!, THE END?, HALT!, YOU!, BONK!, YOURS!, and the banner WARDAN'S MARKET; default used: all included (about 16, can be cut to 10).

Small comic additions: the shop boy drowning in the apron, the porter walking past the hidden Wardan, the fake 'THE END?' thought before the gate, two soldiers failing to push the door inside the caliph's thought cloud, the soldiers bumping helmets; default used: all included.
The enchanted hoard's 'traits of Wardan' are shown as a scroll checklist (cap, moustache, cleaver) and a glowing hand mark on the door that fits his hand; default used: this invention.
Transition card text is NEXT MORNING... instead of LATER... at 41.34 s; default used: NEXT MORNING...

SCRIPT: P3 Arabic ends with 'اختبأ وردان حتى رحل الحمال، واقترب من المكان' (Wardan hid until the porter left, then approached), which has no English translation; the third English chunk will sit under that sentence.
SCRIPT: P4 Arabic says he found a stone door leading to an underground room, while the English says 'Through an opening he saw an underground room' (the stone door is missing in English).
SCRIPT: P5 Arabic says 'when sleep overcame the woman and the bear' and 'killed the bear with his knife'; the English says 'When both lay exhausted' and omits the knife.
